title: Ghost Lights Commission
summary: Since the crate found its first word, Dax's night watch has logged pale lights along the boundary-mountain line — too steady for storm fire, too high for lanterns, and last night they kept *time*: three-two-three. The gauge needs eyes on the rim that aren't its keeper's. Hold station at two rim posts after dark, log the lights' measure, and don't answer anything that answers you.

objectives.label: Hold station under the boundary wall at the old finish gantry — let the watch-meter settle
Hold at Dax's gauge deck — log the lights' measure
Leave the watch log in the survey camp courier box

offer.text: Courier. Since your cargo went conversational — don't ask how the gauge knows a thing has a voice; the gauge reads everything that hums — my night watch has logged lights on the boundary-mountain line. Pale. Lunar-coloured. Steady in my good glass, which is the part I don't care for.

Storm fire flickers. Lanterns swing. These do neither, and last night — I'm not telling the chart this, the chart sulks — they kept *time*. Three-two-three. I need eyes on the rim that aren't mine. Mine have a conflict of interest: they panic at beauty. Been reliable about it for forty seasons.
You want me to stand still in the dark and stare at the haunted end of the map.
Calibrated summary. The pay is honest and the coffee is tar-grade. Refusal goes in the register under 'sensible'. Nobody ever opens that page.

accept.text: Two stations. Hold under the boundary wall at the old finish gantry first — let the watch-meter settle, engine dead. Then my gauge deck; I've set out a fresh chart and the good glass. Count the measure if they keep one. Do NOT count aloud, and do not answer anything that answers you. After: the log goes in the courier box at the survey camp. If I'm asleep, station policy holds that I am awake.

Pem on band nine, station. Word reaches me of lights that count. Attend: if they count in threes, that is *prosody*, and prosody is a claim of authorship. Write down the counts, exactly, in order. History forgives the superstitious — but it quotes the precise, station, forever, out loud.

Ketch. Ridge flats at night, kid: the salt holds the starlight and hides the rifts. Beam low, follow the morse winks, and when the gauge lamp blinks twice you're his problem — the good kind. Also your crate's been quiet all week and I don't believe in coincidences that timed.

complete.text: Log's in. Three-two-three, then a wait, then three-two-three again. I checked the barometer twice, the way you check a pulse. Courier — you saw it too, so I'll write it plain: the parallax is *wrong*. Those lights aren't on the mountains. They're beyond the wall, and beyond the wall is on no chart I'm paid to trust.

Page six of your own log. Your own hand. 'It hummed back.' Commission is filed complete; the finding is filed under 'pressure's holding', which is what this station writes when nothing is holding. Take the pay. Take the coffee. Forget the coffee.
It hummed the same count back. Three-two-three. I didn't tell it to. I didn't tell it anything.

Nobody told the desert either, rider, and the desert's been practising. Night hatch rule applies: knock twice, state the weather you want. I want rain. Logged. 'Pressure's holding.' Off you go — and if the lights say your name out there, that's the wind showing off. Keep riding.
